task.title: Reconstruct Ilya V2 hardware-run pipetting parameters
primary_questions: Which pipetting-wizard calibration files were actually selected during non-simulated Ilya V2 experiments?
What effective pipetting parameters were used for every component and requested volume?

notes: The workflow supplies the base liquid type to aspirate_from_vial and dispense_into_wellplate.
The vial/component name retains the _dye suffix, but the liquid argument does not.
The robot library and pipetting wizard therefore control the final file lookup and effective parameters.

historical_findings_to_verify.reason: Prior repository inspection indicated that the dye calibration files, relevant workflow changes, and SIMULATE=False appeared together around June 11.

excluded_evidence.reason: The located timing artifacts completed three rounds in only a few seconds and were identified as simulation runs. They do not prove hardware parameters.

historical_findings_to_verify.warning: Do not report candidate filenames as experimentally confirmed unless the hardware logs or an exact run-era source snapshot establish them.

run_identification: Identify every actual execution of workflows/ilya_workflow_v2.py.
Report each log filename and timestamp plus evidence that real hardware was controlled.
Determine which run produced the final experimental data, if the evidence permits.
file_selection: Extract the exact calibration file path selected for each liquid type.
Retain raw matching messages, timestamps, logger names, and source log filenames.
Report whether different runs selected different paths or file versions.
effective_parameters: Extract actual wizard output or robot method arguments for requested volumes 70, 100, and 150 uL.

Capture every logged aspiration and dispensing parameter, including speed, acceleration, wait time, cycles, air gap, overaspiration, correction or compensation, heights, retract settings, and any other effective fields.
Distinguish requested volume from adjusted, measured, or commanded volume.
Prefer logged runtime values over values inferred from current CSV files.
source_reconstruction: Identify the exact source revision used for each hardware run when possible.
Explain the wizard lookup algorithm: filename matching, row selection, interpolation, defaults, and workflow-level overrides.
Compare logged values with calibration CSV files as they existed on the experiment date, not only current working-tree contents.

evidence_policy.confirmed: Directly supported by a real hardware-run log or an exact run-era artifact tied to that run.
evidence_policy.inferred: Reconstructed from run-era source or calibration data but not explicitly recorded in the hardware log.
prohibitions: Do not use current calibration-file contents as proof of historical contents.
Do not treat simulated timing logs as hardware evidence.
Do not silently substitute a candidate filename for a logged filename.

desired_deliverables: A machine-readable table containing all 18 required rows.
A concise summary of which wizard files are hardware-log confirmed.
Raw evidence excerpts sufficient to audit each confirmed conclusion.
A list of unresolved issues, especially mutable file lookups or missing historical versions.
